answer: Recursive zero-knowledge reputation commitments and verifiable delay primitives form a resilient security framework, analogous to a canyon carved by the relentless spiral of time, impeding the computational feasibility of identity cloning. By iteratively committing to a reputation graph, agents embed their past actions, rendering any attempt to forge a new identity a futile fable, as the accumulated evidence of their past behavior serves as an unforgeable proof of their identity, thereby ensuring the authenticity of their claims.
